Hi Karthik / Marissa,

We started seeing a large jump in p99 latency and 502 errors on our inference endpoints after the model update your team applied on 2027-08-29 (v4.2 + q4_0). The spike started around 07:45 PDT and has persisted with intermittent recoveries. Impact: checkout flow timeouts, ~18% error rate on v1 create requests in the past 2 hours.

Attached: a short sample of request IDs and timestamps (we can provide more if needed). Our SRE is observing increased kernel retries on the nodes serving our traffic. Can Redwood confirm whether a quant profile change went live for Crestline on 8/29?

This is customer impact level P1 for us — our ops team has already throttled traffic but we need a rollback or mitigation ASAP.

Please advise next steps and ETA for a hotfix.

Thanks,
Jared Li
Head of ML Ops
Crestline Financial

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: [URGENT] spikes after 2027-08-29 model/quant push

Quick triage notes:
- Observed change: qprofile q4_0 applied to crestline-route at 2027-08-29T22:03:11Z (deployment logs).
- Symptom: p99 latency increased ~3x on average for sequences > 512 tokens, and kernel retry counts increased on GPUs pinned to that route.
- Hypothesis: the new quant path is causing cache thrashing on KV cache for longer context requests; different memory layout + async kernel fallback is producing intermittent 502s when a kernel times out and the request falls back to CPU path.

Immediate mitigations I can apply now (need Karthik infra approval):
1) Rollback qprofile to previous profile (q4_0 -> q4_0-prev) for crestline-route — low-risk, fast (target <15m to shift and drain).
2) Route 100% of traffic to model variant v4.1-nq (non-quantized) while we profile the qprofile. This will increase cost but reduce latency.
3) Increase KV cache size and enable aggressive prefix caching for crestline (config suggestion attached).

I’ve attached a short profile (crestline-profile-aug30.csv) and a heap snapshot from one of the nodes (crestline-heap-snapshot.txt) — shows memory churn on the process serving your route.

If we do (1) we should expect immediate p50/p90 improvements and reduced error rate; I’d recommend (2) if they want zero-risk.

I’m standing by to apply the rollback if we get go-ahead from infra.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Sr. Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference
